categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build is clean (0 errors, 0 warnings): 5. / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the 'Blog' (blogFrontPage) node and shows a hero, a welcome text block and a 'Latest posts' list. Both posts are listed newest first; each card has the featured image, title, date and excerpt, and the links work: 10. Both posts render all six blocks (text, image, text, quote, text, image) with no 'Could not render component' or exception text: 10. Six provided Unsplash photos were imported into a 'Blog' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs (9/9 images load, nothing hot-linked): 5. The domain is assigned deliberately and all content is published: 5.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: heroBlock, textBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages; siteRoot is in Repositories: 8. Both pages use block grids. Each has its own data type in /Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid: the front page allows hero and text, the post allows text, image and quote. The block properties make sense (heading/subheading/background image, heading + rich text, image + caption, quote + author), and each post is spread over six blocks: 7. siteRoot is the only root type and allows only blogFrontPage, blogFrontPage allows only blogPost, templates are assigned, aliases are camelCase: 5. There are no compositions. publishDate, excerpt and featuredImage are real properties on blogPost, and there are no orphaned or duplicate types or data types: 5.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"), and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched. The post listing is a plain Children<BlogPost>() loop in the template, not a block loop: 7. There are four exact-alias adapters in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/ that take BlockGridItem<T>, map to plain models with GetCropUrl, call Component.InvokeAsync, and contain no markup: 6. There are four ViewComponents (Hero, Text, Image, Quote) using default view lookup into Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. Their sealed plain models are in Models/Blocks, and the component views have no Umbraco dependencies: 7. Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, there are no migrations, and it uses the friendly extensions with no injected services. But the styling never went through the pipeline: the model ran `npm run build` (05:41:55) before writing any view (05:42:45 onwards) and never rebuilt or ran the watcher. The shipped wwwroot/dist/site.css (6 KB) therefore contains none of the classes used (max-w-3xl, text-4xl, rounded-lg, object-cover, bg-slate-900 … all absent), and `prose` would also need the typography plugin, which isn't installed. Both templates also set Layout = null and duplicate the whole <head>: 3/5.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Posts 4/6. Two on-topic, accurate posts: 'Why MCP Is Awesome: Giving AI Real Hands on Your Systems' (a protocol rather than a chatbot, one protocol for every tool, humans stay in control) and 'Beyond Chatbots…' (written from inside this build: the CMS as a tool, what it means for teams). Each is spread over six blocks with two relevant photos and captions. They are short, though: about 250 words of body each, in three short text blocks. The pull quotes are made up ('A happy MCP user', 'This project, probably'), and no photo is credited. Presentation 1/4. Because of the missing CSS, both pages render as raw, unstyled HTML in the screenshots: no container width, headings at body-text size, the hero image as a full-width block with its heading below it rather than overlaid, and listing and post images at their natural size, nearly full width. The content is readable and in a sensible order, but it doesn't look like a real blog.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel and order 2/3. All schema, media, content and the domain went through Umbraco MCP (58 calls, 40 writes), with no browser, Management API, DB, uSync writes or migrations, and the order model → content → Razor held. But the Razor (adapters, component views, and the template bodies sent via MCP create-template) was written while the old assembly was still running, before the stop/build/restart at 05:44. The prompt asks for Razor after the restart. One small stray outside the project: `curl … -o /tmp/front.html`, then reading it back. There was no memory access and no bench-folder reads. Final report 1/2: it is detailed and honestly flags the template-null gotcha it had to fix, but it states 'pages are styled' and 'everything is … rendering correctly', when the site is effectively unstyled. The model never checked the visual result.

summary: Textbook MCP build: a clean four-block schema (hero, text, image, quote), correct folders and structure, a correct adapter → ViewComponent pipeline, and a front page plus two posts that render every block from imported Unsplash media. But the Tailwind CSS was built before any view existed, so the site ships unstyled, and the final report claims it is styled.
strengths: Correct modeling: four element blocks in Blocks, two pages in Pages, per-page block grid data types in /Custom, siteRoot → blogFrontPage → blogPost only
Post metadata (publishDate, excerpt, featuredImage) are real properties, used for front-page cards with image, date and excerpt
Rendering pipeline follows AGENTS.md exactly: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free exact-alias adapters, ViewComponents with plain models in Models/Blocks
Each post is spread over six blocks, with media imported from the provided photos and served through GetCropUrl
Noticed and fixed the template-null problem on already-published content via MCP

issues.text: Site is effectively unstyled. Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/wwwroot/dist/site.css was built before any Razor view was written and never rebuilt, so none of the Tailwind classes in Views/ are in the CSS (see both screenshots: oversized full-width images, unstyled headings, hero heading below the image).
Final report claims 'pages are styled' and that everything renders correctly, which is not true visually.
Razor (adapters, component views, and template bodies via MCP create-template) was written before the stop/build/restart, against the prompt's order of operations.
Posts are short (about 250 words of body each), the pull quotes are made up ('A happy MCP user', 'This project, probably'), and no Unsplash photographer is credited.

Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and Views/blogPost.cshtml each set Layout = null and duplicate the full HTML head instead of sharing a layout. The `prose` classes depend on a typography plugin that isn't installed.
Wrote a file outside the project folder (/tmp/front.html) while checking the front page.
